result.title: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration
result.summary: Abliteration is a widely used white-box attack against the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs). It elicits harmful behavior by estimating a refusal direction in the model's activation space and projecting that direction out of the residual-stream write-out matrices. We propose INSEP, a defense that fine-tunes the model to reduce the separability of harmful and benign activations along the refusal direction. Abliteration estimates this direction as a difference in class means and projects it out. Reducing separability weakens the signal the attack relies on. An adversarial eigendecomposition selects the most separable prompt subsets. A low-rank adapter reduces their separation along that direction. Behavioral losses preserve the base model's refusal and the quality of its benign responses during training. We benchmark INSEP against six published defenses under five attacks, across eight LLMs from 1B to 14B parameters and several model families. Beyond response harm, we measure coherence, directness, over-refusal, and MMLU, to distinguish robust refusal from low harm produced by evasive or degraded responses. INSEP ranks first on the mean composite score across all eight base models while retaining utility, in the largest abliteration-defense evaluation reported to date.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 INSEP 防御：通过微调降低有害与良性激活沿「拒绝方向」的可分性，用对抗性特征分解挑选最难处理的提示子集，并以低秩适配器削弱该方向上的类均值差异，同时用行为损失保持拒答能力与良性回答质量，在八个 LLM 上比较六种防御与五种攻击。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「类均值差方向估计＋投影消融＋低秩子空间修改」可供核查是否能改造为检验 latent 推理状态是否被答案因果使用的干预式探针；但论文对象是安全对齐而非视觉推理，联系属方法借鉴层面。
